svg.text: Capture setup — what goes above the box, and how high

NeoBox is a flash light-source box for camera-scanning 35 mm and 120 film. It fixes the film plane about 120.3 mm above the table; above that line sit your camera, your lens, and one dimension only you can supply.
A — the rig in elevation, drawn to scale
Flash inside, firing sideways at the far wall;
the film is lit from below through the
Aiming the lens at the centre of
the frame is not the same as
being parallel to it. The sensor
must be parallel to the film
plane, or one edge of the frame
will be sharp and the other soft.
Copy stand, or a tripod with a horizontal / reversible centre column. Camera looks straight down.
Macro lens. Working distance belongs to the lens, not the box. Measure it once, mark the column.
Film plane, about 120.3 mm above the table — fixed. Changing format does not move it.
The imaging cone from the film up into the lens. Keep arms, cables and hands out of it.
Parallel, not merely aimed — see the note at the right, and check it with the mirror in panel B.
B — the mirror method: parallel, or merely pointed?
plane on top of the holder.
Look in live view. You see the lens
is parallel to the film plane.
Then trim the three stage nuts — front = pitch, rear pair = roll — and check again. Parallelism
first, evenness second: a flash freezes vibration but it cannot fix a tilted film plane.
C — magnification needed to fill the sensor
Any 1:1 macro lens covers every format in this table — for the bigger formats you simply use less than full
0.43× is the 6×6-on-full-frame case. It is the magnification at which the dust calculation in
check that your body actually fires
the flash in the shutter mode you use

Box geometry from cad/neobox.blend; film-plane height from docs/design.md; the magnification table from docs/scanning.md. Camera, lens, stand and hot-shoe transmitter are not part of the project and are not in the build cost.
